name.en: Psychological type (four preference pairs, after Jung)
name.ru: Психологический тип (четыре пары предпочтений, по мотивам Юнга)

summary.en: Preferences on four pairs of poles, combined into a type that the person checks by best fit. Genuine MBTI® results are recorded only through their instrument entries. E/I, S/N and T/F follow Jung's attitudes and functions; treating them as four independent preference pairs and adding J/P is the Briggs–Myers operationalisation.
summary.ru: Предпочтения на четырёх парах полюсов, складывающиеся в тип, который человек проверяет по принципу «лучшего соответствия». Подлинные результаты MBTI® записываются только через карточки инструментов. E/I, S/N и T/F следуют установкам и функциям Юнга; трактовка их как четырёх независимых пар предпочтений и добавление пары J/P — операционализация Бриггс и Майерс.

mentalModel.summary: People show preferences on four pairs of poles; a type is a starting point that the person checks by best fit, not a verdict.
assumptions: a type is a convenient summary of four preferences
the person is the authority on best fit
the underlying measures are continuous even when a type is reported
mentalModel.unitOfAnalysis: the person's preferences across typical situations
attendsTo: situations where the opposite pole shows
mentalModel.howChangeHappens: Preferences are treated as relatively stable; the person may revise the best-fit type at any time.
mentalModel.languageGuidance: Speak of preferences, never of fixed kinds of people; use the person's own type wording; never call a quiz result an MBTI® type.

do: show pole clarity when it is available
dont: assign a type to the person
label any non-MBTI® result with the MBTI® marks

exploratoryQuestions: In which situations does the other pole show?
helperMustNot: derive a type from Big Five or other scores
present a type as evidence of fit for a role, task or team
doesNotClaim: that people fall into distinct types
riskNotes: Type labels invite pigeon-holing and are misused in hiring
Branded type labels are protected marks; generic results must never carry them

toolkit.name: Best-fit check
toolkit.description: Read short descriptions of each pole in your own words and choose the one that fits best; note where neither fits.
cautions: The result is self-identified, not measured

toolkit.name: Record a genuine instrument result
toolkit.description: Record the type and pole clarity from a genuine MBTI® assessment, with the trademark notice; never the report prose.

representations.description: Four-letter type with clarity per pole and whether the person confirmed it by best fit.

suggestionRequires: the person asked for ways of describing preferences

citations.note: McCrae & Costa 1989 (N = 267 men, 201 women): no support for truly dichotomous preferences or distinct types; the instrument measures four relatively independent dimensions

citations.ref: Pittenger 1993, as cited in a secondary source
citations.note: Between 39% and 76% of respondents received a different type on retest after five weeks [verify]

citations.ref: The Myers-Briggs Company, Trademark Guidelines, guideline 5
citations.note: Use the MBTI marks only for genuine MBTI products and services; other instruments must not be described with them. Revision date of the guidelines to be re-checked

citations.ref: Myers & McCaulley 1985, Manual: A Guide to the Development and Use of the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator, as cited in a secondary source
citations.note: The judging–perceiving preference was added by Briggs and Myers; Jung's typology has the two attitudes and four functions

evidence.notes: Evidence about the instrument's dimensions is not evidence that people fall into types.

supports: self-description in a vocabulary the person chose
talking about preferences the person recognises
doesNotEstablish: that the person belongs to a distinct type
